### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/dogfood`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **201** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/dogfood/package.json`, `packages/qa/dogfood/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**48** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/dogfood/package.json`, `packages/qa/dogfood/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **20** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **49** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5e7f87ba69a2b56e846b8fe6e61d5204a296e616` — the merge of head `4f64bc83a9eec296c06d8fe58adae6d910c6a39d` into base `e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5e7f87ba69a2b56e846b8fe6e61d5204a296e616 && git checkout 5e7f87ba69a2b56e846b8fe6e61d5204a296e616
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f 4f64bc83a9eec296c06d8fe58adae6d910c6a39d && git checkout -B drift-repro e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f && git merge --no-ff 4f64bc83a9eec296c06d8fe58adae6d910c6a39d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Epic red-line review of #32239 (#31696 PR-1a, flow slots per package) at head 4f64bc83: ~~PASS~~ WITHDRAWN.**

> **[Edit: I withdraw this PASS.]** Seat 1's contract review 6769600058 found M1 on this head, a red-line-1 path I missed. The engine decides that a name is "shared" by counting its slots, but the resolver reads the registry's holders. So when one holder's body is refused at registration, the other holder's arm lands alone under the bare key. A P1 caller then runs P2's flow, and the bare doors serve it instead of answering 409. One shared predicate is owed, with a pin. I will re-read the patch head. The reading below stands for every other path.

**(Original text, at head 4f64bc83:)** I read the diff against main for the slot table, `placeFlowSlot`, the seal and bind path, `flow-precedence.ts` and the activation projection. I did not run anything; the ablation evidence is from the PR body. Contract review and ACCEPT are seat 1's. This head supersedes my withdrawn PASS on #32091.

- **M2 is closed.** The cold-boot bind no longer depends on registration order.
  - `placeFlowSlot` binds a package-less disable row to the incumbent only when `flowHoldersSealed` is set. Before the seal, it calls `refusePackagelessBind`: the row reads as one first read under two holders, so both stay off, one warning is logged, and the row is never bound later.
  - The plugin seals at `kernel:bootstrapped`. In both kernels that fires after `kernel:ready` (`kernel.ts` :619/:632, `lite-kernel.ts` :146/:153), so installed packages arrive before the seal.
  - The three real-kernel boot orders over SQLite, and A9, pin it.
  - After the seal, the bind is durable and awaited. Until it lands, the row keeps every holder off, and a failed write keeps both off.
- **Red line 1, never loosen: holds.**
  - `resolveSlotPrecedence` places a declared override only in the slot of the owner it overrides: `classifyContender` asks `isServedOverrideRowOf(…, owner)`.
  - An environment row over two holders overlays neither and is never armed. This is D4, since there is no single holder for it to customize.
  - An override arm with no holder under two slots is refused (N1, A14).
  - A stored run resumes only on its own package's flow (R8). An older replica fails it as unresumable and never continues on the other package's flow.
- **Red line 2, never guess: holds.**
  - Every bare door answers a two-holder name with `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` naming both.
  - The composition with no resolver refuses where it used to pick by precedence. That is narrowing (1), covered by 6764658726.
  - A credential source that does not declare `readsByPackage` is never asked for a shared slot (S3, A13).
  - A credential write that would touch a row under a shared name is refused before anything is written (M3, A11/A12).
- **Red line 3, releasable: holds.**
  - With one holder, keys, log lines and answers are unchanged. Stored runs gain `flow_package`, as declared.
  - Both narrowings carry FROM→TO and the ADR-0087 marker, and the widening beside them (each package's flow armed in its own slot) is declared.
  - Install still refuses a second holder until PR-3. Until then, every fail-closed limit can be reached only through a sealed clash.

**Owed by later parts of the card** (recorded on #31527's ledger, not charged to this head):
- **PR-1b:** R9 by package, with `readsByPackage = true`.
- **PR-2:** triggers per slot, and the approvals reads of S2, which are fail-closed until then.
- **PR-3, before it makes two holders an authorable state:**
  - N2: a slot whose entry vanished while another package holds the name must not linger until the next `metadata:reloaded`;
  - the mixed-version ledger read (6764387209 item 2);
  - the stale skills parenthetical;
  - the S4 report rows.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published contract on `main`: both declared narrowings make the contract's own refusal real (red line 2, ADR-0150 D3) and take no declared capability away at a consumer. No finding on the narrowings themselves. The must-fix is in the widening beside them.

**M1 — must-fix — "is this name shared" is read off the engine's slot count, and the resolver reads it off the registry's holders. When the two disagree, the surviving slot is treated as the name's one holder, and a caller of the other package is handed it.**

- How the state arises. `registerFlow` runs `canonicalizeFlow` and `registrationChecks` (`engine.ts` :5080) before `placeFlowSlot` (:5089). For a sealed clash of P1:f and P2:f, a body of P1 that is refused there leaves no slot for P1. P2's arm carries `holder`, so `placeFlowSlot` skips E1 (:4779) and files P2's flow under the bare key `f`. The plugin's failure paths do the same (`plugin.ts` :5613, :5721: only the failing winner's own slot is withdrawn). The registry still holds two packages under `f`.
- On `main` this state cannot exist: E1 at `registerFlow` refused every arm of a name the resolver refuses, so the engine held nothing under `f` and every door answered "not found".
- What the tree does in that state:
  - **A P1 caller runs P2's flow.** `resolveFlowKey` (:4959) takes the not-shared branch, asks the resolver for caller P1, gets "resolved, own package" (`package-scoped-resolver.ts` step 1: P1 holds `f` in the registry), and returns `{ key: name }`. `executeKey` then runs the one body filed under `f`, which is P2's. A `subflow` or `map` node in any P1 flow that names `f` dispatches P2's flow. That is red line 1 ("no environment-wide guess for a caller with a package"): the resolver said P1's item and the engine served another package's.
  - **The bare doors serve P2's flow instead of refusing.** `bareFlowKey` (:4984) returns the bare key, so `getFlow`, `toggleFlow`, `withdrawFlow`, `unregisterFlow`, the version history and the rollback act on P2's flow under a name the registry says two packages hold. The contract is 409 naming both (carry-in 6760047493, "Readers before narrowing").
  - **The by-name owner reads can answer the other package.** For a slot that is not shared, `packagedFlowOwner` (:5557) asks the loader by name alone, and `packagedArtifactOwner` (`protocol-write-gates.ts` :452) answers one shipper of a two-shipper name. That value feeds `armedFlowPackage` (the caller package every reference in P2's body resolves from), the ledger projection's `holderOf` (:2882), and the package a toggle's durable row names (`flow-definitions.ts` `toggleFlow`), so a switch of P2's flow can be written as P1's row.
  - **The slot is armed on its trigger under the bare name** (the decline at :4033 is keyed on the same count). Each fire is then refused by the resolver, so it fails closed, noisily. The changeset's sentence "the only new way a flow of a sealed-clash name runs in this release is a `subflow` or `map` call from a flow of its own package" does not hold here.
  - `flowRefusals.delete(name)` on P2's registration (:5109 and the line above it) erases P1's recorded refusal of the same bare name, so `getFlowRegistration('f')` reads `registered` and nothing reports the state.
- No test in the diff holds two registry holders with one engine slot. "its removal moves them back" pins the move to the bare key as correct, with no resolver attached.
- Fix: one predicate for "shared", used by every reader that asks it. A name is shared when two slots hold it **or** the resolver refuses it for a caller with no package (`flowHolder(name)` refused), which is the predicate the credential write guard already uses. A holder-named arm keeps its qualified key while that is so; the not-shared branch of `resolveFlowKey` must not answer a package caller with a slot of another package; and a slot with a package asks the loader the per-package question. Pin: two registry holders, one body refused, then a P1 caller's subflow call, the bare doors and a toggle. See ③ for the size consequence.

**S1 — should-fix — every `http` node of a shared-slot flow is refused, including one with no signing secret, and neither carrier says so.**
For a source that does not read by package, the wrapper's `holds` answers `true` for a shared slot (`engine.ts` :5795). `http-nodes.ts` :241 then always calls `resolveFlowCredential`, which throws, and the node is refused with "its signing secret is held by the flow credential store and could not be read". That is fail closed and it is what the S3 ruling implies, but the changeset declares only "a credential read ... is refused": an unsigned `http` node in such a flow also stops until PR-1b, unless it authors `signingSecret: ''`. Declare it beside the S3 sentence, and correct the node's sentence for this case (nothing is known to be held).

**N1 — nit — the declared-limits census names `plugin-approvals` only.** The runtime's bare `getFlow` readers (`flow-dispatch-status.ts` :161, `flow-start-admission.ts`, the `/automation` domain doors) get the same 409 for a sealed-clash name. Fail closed, PR-3's doors own them; list them.

**N2 — nit — `listHistory` applies `limit` before the slot filter** (`flow-slot-run-store.ts` :66), so a shared slot's history can come back shorter than asked while more rows of its own exist.

**N3 — nit — the skill parenthetical** (`SKILL.md` :76, "an older clash, never armed") is stale from this PR on. The refusal it teaches is unchanged and no author can create the state before PR-3; the carry to PR-3 is accepted.

**N4 — nit — the changeset's export list** omits `FlowContender.holder`, `FlowPrecedenceWinner.holder` and `packagedFlowSlotOwner`, which the PR body lists.

The earlier record's findings (6764624467), judged on this tree:

- **M1 (declarations, routing): fixed.** One declaration on both carriers (②); the narrowing's authority is recorded by the epic (6764658726 item 1); the battery is reported at the head.
- **M2 (bind by boot order): fixed.** `placeFlowSlot` binds only when `flowHoldersSealed` (:4798) and otherwise calls `refusePackagelessBind` (:4801), which marks the row as first read under two holders: both off, one warning, never bound later (`flow-activation-projection.ts`). The seal is set at `kernel:bootstrapped` (`plugin.ts` :2676), which the kernel triggers after `kernel:ready` (`kernel.ts` :619, :632), so both the pull and the installed-package rehydrate are before it. A row hydrated after both holders arrive is caught by `hasShared`. Pinned at the engine in both orders and over a real kernel in three.
- **M3 (R9 writes): fixed in the PR-1a form the split ruling and its addendum order.** `store()` refuses an explicit value (:334) and any existing row at a position the body no longer keeps (:343) before any write; `promote()` refuses when a draft row exists or an active row would be removed (:454). What passes both guards writes and deletes nothing. `prune` is by name but removes rows only for a state in which no stored row of the name remains. By-package reads and writes are PR-1b's.
- **S1 (Q4 amendment): recorded** on the card (6764658726 item 4, 6764686113) and stated in the changeset.
- **S2 (approvals): declared** as a limit in the changeset, carried to PR-2.
- **S3 (unscoped source): implemented as ruled** (refuse), declared, pinned; see S1 above for its undeclared consequence.
